ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an oxygen-containing cyclic transition-state structure, and the curved arrows need to be ignored. At the bottom an imine fragment is visible: N forms a double bond with the carbon in the ring, and N is also connected to R1; at the lower right there is another separately marked H+. On the ring, clockwise, one can see: the ring oxygen atom connected to the imine carbon, an acetal carbon bearing an exocyclic R4/wildcard substituent and bearing OH, a second ring oxygen atom, and a substituted carbon bearing R2 and R3, finally closing back to the imine carbon. Reasoning: According to the requirements of the problem, write unspecified substituent endpoints such as R1, R2, R3, R4 all as the wildcard *. Starting from the wildcard connected to the imine nitrogen, the imine fragment is written as */N=C1\. Then encode sequentially along the ring as O, C(*)(O), O, C1(*)*, obtaining */N=C1\OC(*)(O)OC1(*)*. The separate proton in the figure is appended as a disconnected species as .[H+].

method.method_draft: First transcribe the atom graph visible in the image, treating R1, R2, R3, R4 and other unspecified substituent termini as wildcard atoms. Start from the wildcard attached to imine nitrogen, encode the imine as `*/N=C1\`, then follow the ring clockwise through `O`, the substituted acetal carbon `C(*)(O)`, the second ring oxygen `O`, and the substituted carbon closing back to the imine carbon as `C1(*)*`. Finally append the separate proton shown in the image as a disconnected species, giving `*/N=C1\OC(*)(O)OC1(*)*.[H+]`.

planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the drawing and ignore the curved arrows. Read a five-membered heterocyclic framework containing an imine fragment: an N bearing R1 is double-bonded to a ring carbon; the ring continues through O, a carbon bearing R2/R3 and an OH/O substituent pattern, another O, and a carbon bearing R4/generic substituents back to the imine carbon. Note the separate H+ drawn near nitrogen and the slash/backslash geometry around the N=C bond.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the task is to give the SMILES expression and to ignore the arrows, so only atoms, bonds, substituent placeholders, stereobond marks, ring closure, and the separate proton are encoded.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: replace each R group or unspecified substituent by wildcard `*`; encode ring closure with the same ring number `1`; encode the N=C alkene/iminium geometry with `/` and `\`; write a disconnected proton as `.[H+]`; omit all curved-arrow information because arrows are not part of the molecular graph.
